moa: Afatinib is an irreversible ErbB family tyrosine kinase inhibitor that covalently binds to EGFR, HER2, and HER4, blocking their kinase activity and downstream signaling pathways such as MAPK and PI3K/AKT, leading to growth inhibition and apoptosis in EGFR-addicted tumors.

REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_EGFR_IN_CANCER.description: Regulates EGFR signaling involved in cell proliferation and survival.
REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_EGFR_IN_CANCER.interpretation: EGFR signaling is crucial in driving proliferation in EGFR-mutant cancers.

BIOCARTA_ERK_PATHWAY.description: Involves ERK signaling in cell proliferation and differentiation.
BIOCARTA_ERK_PATHWAY.interpretation: ERK pathway activation contributes to cancer cell proliferation.

KEGG_MEDICUS_REFERENCE_HGF_MET_RAS_ERK_S.description: Involves HGF/MET signaling leading to RAS and ERK activation.
KEGG_MEDICUS_REFERENCE_HGF_MET_RAS_ERK_S.interpretation: MET signaling can bypass EGFR inhibition, contributing to resistance.

REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_VEGF.interpretation: VEGF signaling supports tumor angiogenesis and growth.

BIOCARTA_AKT_PATHWAY.description: Involves AKT signaling in cell survival and metabolism.
BIOCARTA_AKT_PATHWAY.interpretation: AKT pathway activation supports cancer cell survival and resistance.

notes: Limited data on breast cancer-specific pathways; see citations for lung cancer context.
